answer: Use insurer-backed identity bonds. First, an applicant buys a $500 surety bond from an insurer that checks a government ID and a video call. Second, the insurer posts the bond on the ledger, tied to one hardware key, so one person cannot hold two bonds. Third, if the identity proves fake, the insurer pays $10,000 to harmed parties and revokes it. Forging 1,000 identities costs $500,000 in premiums plus 14 days of underwriting each, and insurers blacklist fraudsters. Like a wharf with a single narrow inlet, only verified ships dock; a marble seal, once cracked, cannot be quietly recarved.
